title: Client state batching and recall protocol (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal sketch for a lightweight client-side batching and recall protocol intended to: reduce token overhead, allow quick rehydration of short-lived local LLM sessions, and provide an extensible wire format that works with Redwood hosted/dedicated runtimes and edge proxies.

Design goals (informal):
- Minimize round trips and per-token cost for interactive clients (mobile/desktop/web).
- Allow partial rehydration: answerers should be able to request only 'most-recent-turns' or semantic anchors.
- Support lossy, loseless, and hybrid recall strategies.
- Work with streaming responses and KV cache re-use on the runtime side.

High-level flow (ASCII):
Client -> Edge SDK (local) -> Edge Proxy -> Redwood Runtime
   |             |                 |
   +---(batched)-->  append -> store/queue -> smart-route -> model
   |             |                 |
   +<--(recall)----  recall <- fetch/cache <- fallback

Key concepts:
- Envelope: a small wrapper for client state units (turns, embeddings, metadata).
- Chunk: an Envelope payload up to ~4KB (configurable). Multiple chunks may be appended in one call.
- Anchors: lightweight semantic fingerprints (e.g. embedding id) that enable semantic recall without full text.
- RecallPolicy: client-declared hints for what to retrieve on reconnect.

Wire API sketch (HTTP/JSON over TLS; also supports gRPC):
1) Append: POST /v1/client-context/append
   Headers: Authorization: Bearer <session-token>
   Body: {
     "session_id": "s_12345",
     "chunks": [
       {"chunk_id":"c1","ts":1699012345,"type":"turn","payload":"base64(...)","anchors":["a_e1"]},
       {"chunk_id":"c2","ts":1699012349,"type":"meta","payload":"base64(...)"}
     ],
     "max_batch_tokens": 512  // hint for server batching scheduler
   }
   Response: {"ingest_id":"ing_99","accepted":2,"queued":true}

2) Recall: POST /v1/client-context/recall
   Body: {
     "session_id":"s_12345",
     "policy": {"mode":"hybrid","window_turns":6,"anchors":true,"max_tokens":800},
     "preferred_forms":["compact","text-first"]
   }
   Response: {
     "result": [
       {"chunk_id":"c1","type":"turn","payload":"base64(...)","reason":"recent"},
       {"chunk_id":"c_anchor_5","type":"anchor","anchor":"a_e1","reason":"semantic_match"}
     ],
     "continuation_token":"cont_xxx"
   }

Edge SDK responsibilities (client-side):
- Coalesce user actions into chunks (debounce, combine small quick edits).
- Maintain local LRU for ephemeral items (unsent) and checkpoint durable receipts from Append responses.
- Retry Append with exponential backoff; if offline, persist to local SQLite/LevelDB until reconnect.
- On reconnect, call Recall with policy tuned to the UX (e.g., last 8 turns + anchors).

Server-side behavior (runtime/edge-proxy):
- Append validates envelope signatures (optional) and writes to in-memory prioritized queue and cold store (object storage) depending on retention policy.
- Batcher groups Append payloads by session_id (when possible) and by model/tenant affinity to reduce KV cache warm-up.
- Recall consults cache first: returns cached chunk payloads inline when small, otherwise returns references (uri + signed url) plus advisory metadata for streaming.
- Smart routing: if the request includes anchors and runtime has embedding index, do a fast ANN lookup and return minimal anchor matches.

Chunk schema (draft):
- chunk_id: string (client- or server-generated)
- ts: unix seconds
- type: one of [turn, system, meta, anchor, embedding]
- payload: base64 bytes (optional, can be empty when chunk is anchor-only)
- anchors: [string] optional list of anchor ids
- sig: optional HMAC for tamper detection (HMAC-SHA256 of chunk_id|ts|payload)

Example chunk (before base64) for a user turn:
{
  "chunk_id": "c_20251103_01",
  "ts": 176 {
    // intentionally small placeholder in draft; real schema uses ints
  }
}

Config knobs (client config + server policy):
- max_batch_tokens (client hint): target tokens to aim for when triggering append batching.
- recall_window_turns: how many of the most recent turns to pull back by default.
- anchor_threshold: similarity threshold for returning anchors.
- retention_ttl: how long to keep chunks in fast store before cold-move.
- eviction_policy: [lru, ttl, size_based, semantic] (semantic = drop low-utility chunks by score)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do anchors belong in Append or should they be computed server-side from text payloads? (Tradeoffs: client cost vs server index freshness)
- How large should a chunk be? Very small chunks increase metadata overhead; large chunks hurt incremental recall.
- Privacy: allow clients to mark chunks as non-persistent or local-only — semantics for private/sensitive data.
- Client versioning: need schema version field and migration path for older clients.
- Rate limiting: how to enforce per-client budget while allowing bursts for real-time UX.

Interoperability notes with Redwood products:
- Hosted API: default retention_ttl = 7 days on fast store, anchors persisted to tenant index.
- Dedicated: admin can set retention and cold-store S3 path; allow on-prem KMS to sign anchors if required.
- Private: edge SDK can be configured to never send 'private' chunks upstream; instead keep local only and rely on on-device cache warming.

Implementation roadmap (personal sprint sketch):
1) Prototype client Append/Recall SDK (node + small web demo) – store chunks locally, append to a simple express service that persists to Redis + S3 stub. (2 weeks)
2) Add anchor generation (client and server options) and simple ANN using FAISS (PoC). (2 wks)
3) Integration test with streaming response path; verify KV reuse behavior in runtime. (2 wks)
4) Security review: HMAC flows, opt-outs, and retention config surface. (1 wk)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a smaller PRD for UX team: reconnection experience for flaky mobile networks.
- Slack thread with @platform-ops about retention defaults and S3 lifecycle rules.
- Mock up SDK API surface (js/ts) and optional TypeScript types.

References / inspirations:
- Local-first apps literature (e.g., Dat, CRDT approaches) for offline persistence patterns.
- Prior Redwood protos for streaming and KV cache integration (see linked github).

If iterating: push a minimal spec that covers Append + Recall + 2 config knobs (max_batch_tokens, recall_window_turns) and a simple JSON chunk envelope. Keep everything backward compatible by adding schema_version at top of envelope.

-- End of draft notes (E. Cho)
